extra.message: The GraphQL 'pastes' filter argument (attacker-controlled) is interpolated via %-formatting directly into a raw SQL string passed to sqlalchemy text() in result.filter(). An attacker can inject SQL such as "aaa' or 1=1--" to bypass the public/burn filters and read all pastes, or exfiltrate arbitrary data from the SQLite database.

ImportPaste mutation concatenates attacker-controlled scheme/host/port/path into a URL string that is embedded into a shell command 'curl --insecure {url}' executed by helpers.run_cmd (os.popen). The strip_dangerous_characters sanitizer is a no-op in easy mode and only strips ';' and '&' in hard mode, leaving '|', '$()', backticks, and newlines usable for arbitrary OS command execution (confirmed by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_os_injection using path "/ || id").

ImportPaste lets an unauthenticated attacker choose arbitrary scheme, host, port, and path, which the server then fetches with 'curl --insecure'. This is a server-side request forgery: attackers can reach internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints, and non-HTTP schemes supported by curl (e.g., file://) to read local resources, with TLS verification disabled.

resolve_system_diagnostics passes the attacker-controlled 'cmd' argument to helpers.run_cmd (os.popen). The only guard is security.allowed_cmds, which returns True for any command in easy mode, and in hard mode uses a weak startswith allowlist ('echo','ps whoami' [implicit string-concatenation bug at core/security.py:37],'tail') that is bypassed with e.g. 'echo x; id'. This yields arbitrary remote command execution.

resolve_system_debug formats the unauthenticated attacker-controlled 'arg' argument into the shell string 'ps {arg}' and executes it via helpers.run_cmd (os.popen) with no sanitization or allowlisting, allowing arbitrary OS command injection (e.g. arg = '; id' or '$(id)').

save_file() concatenates the attacker-controlled 'filename' argument from the uploadPaste GraphQL mutation (core/views.py:186) directly onto WEB_UPLOADDIR with no sanitization. A filename such as '../../app.py' escapes the upload directory and allows arbitrary file write (and thus potential code execution) on the server.

get_identity() decodes the client-supplied JWT with verify_signature:False and verify_exp:False. Any attacker can forge a token with identity 'admin' (no secret needed) and pass it to the 'me' query (core/views.py:283-296), which then exposes the admin user's cleartext password via resolve_password. This is a complete authentication bypass.

The JWT signing key is hardcoded to the trivially guessable string 'dvga' (app.config["JWT_SECRET_KEY"]). Anyone with access to the source code can forge valid access/refresh tokens for arbitrary identities, enabling authentication bypass.
The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to 'dvga', overwriting the secure random key set on line 10. A known session secret allows forging Flask session cookies and defeats session integrity.

The database seeding logic always assigns the admin account the hardcoded weak password 'changeme' (random_password() selects from a single-element list), and this credential is used for the system_diagnostics command-execution guard. Attackers can trivially guess or read it from source.
The operator account is seeded with the hardcoded password 'password123', a publicly known credential that grants login via the login mutation.

User passwords are stored and compared in cleartext (no hashing anywhere: User.create_user stores the raw password; Login at core/views.py:234 filters on plaintext equality; system_diagnostics compares plaintext). Any database read (e.g., via the SQL injection in resolve_pastes or the users query) immediately exposes all credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: resolve_password returns the real cleartext password whenever info.context.json['identity'] == 'admin'. That identity value is derived from a JWT decoded without signature verification (core/helpers.py:21) and written into the request context in resolve_me (line 291), so any attacker can trigger disclosure of admin credentials.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: EditPaste.mutate performs no authentication or ownership check: any unauthenticated caller can modify the title/content of any paste by supplying its numeric id (insecure direct object reference / missing authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DeletePaste.mutate deletes any paste by attacker-supplied id with no authentication or authorization check, allowing unauthenticated users to destroy arbitrary data (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 'deleteAllPastes' query resolver wipes the entire pastes table (Paste.query.delete()) with no authentication or authorization whatsoever; any anonymous GraphQL client can destroy all application data.

format_custom_error embeds the full Python stack trace (traceback.format_stack / format_exc) and the absolute server-side file path into GraphQL error responses returned to clients. This leaks internal code structure, library versions, and filesystem layout, aiding further attacks (verified by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_stack_trace_errors).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The application raises the interpreter recursion limit to 100000 specifically to tolerate deeply nested/circular GraphQL queries. Combined with depth protection that is disabled in easy mode (core/middleware.py:15), attackers can send deeply nested queries that exhaust stack/CPU and crash the server (denial of service).

The unauthenticated systemUpdate query calls security.simulate_load(), which busy-sleeps in a loop for up to ~50 seconds (core/security.py:8-16) while holding a worker. The cost middleware that would throttle it is bypassed entirely in easy mode, so repeated queries cause resource-exhaustion denial of service.

The /graphql endpoint is configured with batch=True, accepting array-based batch queries with no limit on batch size. Attackers can submit arbitrarily large batches of expensive queries (including the SQLi/cmd-injection/DoS resolvers) in a single HTTP request, amplifying denial of service and brute-force attacks.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: CreatePaste (and UploadPaste/ImportPaste) store attacker-controlled title, content, and User-Agent without any sanitization or output encoding. These values are later rendered into HTML via jQuery .append()/template interpolation in templates/paste.html (lines 132-156), so payloads like '<script>alert(1)</script>' execute in other users' browsers (stored XSS, confirmed by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_xss).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: The /start_over route invokes helpers.initialize(), which shells out to 'python3 setup.py' to delete and rebuild the entire database and upload directory. The route has no authentication, so any remote attacker can reset/destroy all application data at will.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /difficulty/<level> route (and the X-DVGA-MODE header handler at lines 468-475) lets any unauthenticated client flip the server between 'easy' and 'hard' security modes, disabling depth/cost/introspection protections and re-enabling vulnerable behavior (e.g., the no-op command sanitizer) for all users.

The 'env' cookie set by the index route lacks the Secure and HttpOnly attributes. The cookie gates access to the GraphiQL IDE (core/middleware.py:122-124), so its exposure over plaintext HTTP and to JavaScript weakens that access control.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
